items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: there was a kid lived down the street from me, Harry Ballan

ctx.x: Bu-dump-bump is right. But all the things you’ve done, I don’t like to bring myself into this but I can personally relate to cause I’ve done a few of them and I know they have required different talents. You started out playing the piano, right? Did you have a point in your teens where you said to yourself dammit, I’m going to be a musician. I’m going to make a living as a musician?

Well I don’t know how to say it. It was almost like pre-ordained or natural for me that this happened. I’m the youngest of three children and sometimes I think the youngest child they say is spoiled or has more options because maybe the parents had other experiences with the older children or something like that. So I evinced a talent for music early on, not a great talent but just I loved to play and I was always playing. And my high school band director had been a music theory major at Manhattan School of…
wonderful piano, and he was a year younger than me, than I. And so but his parents made him get a law degree. And I think that was probably how it was for most kids, but it wasn’t like that for me.
